common_name: Lilliput Agapanthus (Dwarf Deep Blue Lily of the Nile)

planting.note: Plant container-grown divisions in spring in well-drained soil in full sun; Lilliput is one of the longest-established dwarf agapanthus selections and flowers heavily even when slightly pot-bound.

directions: A long-popular dwarf agapanthus forming a dense clump of slender, grassy deep-green leaves under a foot tall, topped in mid to late summer by compact rounded umbels of deep blue flowers on short sturdy scapes. Its small scale suits containers, rock gardens, and border fronts, and restricted root space tends to encourage heavier flowering rather than suppress it. Grow in full sun in well-drained soil with regular water, and avoid dividing too often since established clumps flower best when slightly congested.

common_name: Summer Skies Agapanthus (Cold-Hardy Pale Blue Lily of the Nile)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in well-drained soil in full sun; Summer Skies was selected from a Headbourne Hybrids strain specifically for improved cold hardiness and tolerates winters considerably colder than most agapanthus.

directions: Selected by Steve Hottovy of Beyond Green in Oregon from a Headbourne Hybrids strain, this deciduous selection bears rounded umbels of pale blue, trumpet-shaped flowers streaked with deeper blue down each petal, carried on strong stalks through midsummer into early fall. Its standout trait is cold hardiness well beyond typical agapanthus. Grow in full sun in well-drained soil with regular moisture, and let the deciduous foliage die back naturally each fall under a protective winter mulch.

common_name: Fireworks Agapanthus (Compact Bicolor White and Violet Lily of the Nile)

planting.note: Plant container-grown starts in spring in well-drained soil in full sun; Fireworks is a patented, compact bicolor selection (US PP #30,162) that won the RHS Award of Garden Merit and an HTA New Plant Award.

directions: A compact evergreen bicolor cultivar with rounded umbels that open as upright white buds and flare into trumpet flowers with deep purple-blue bases and crisp white tips, giving a two-tone starburst look. Short, dense strap foliage stays tidy under two feet while flower scapes rise taller, blooming over an unusually long stretch into early fall. Grow in full sun to light shade in well-drained soil of average fertility; it tolerates sand, chalk, and loam equally well.

common_name: Double Diamond Agapanthus (Dwarf Double White Lily of the Nile)

planting.note: Plant container-grown starts in spring in well-drained soil in full sun to part shade; Double Diamond is a patent-protected dwarf selection (cultivar code 'RFDD') valued for fully double white blooms and an RHS Award of Garden Merit.

directions: A dwarf evergreen cultivar under a foot tall, carrying frilled, fully double white blooms with a ruffled texture quite distinct from the simple trumpet flowers of most agapanthus, held above neat strappy foliage from midsummer into early fall. Its small size and drought tolerance suit patio containers, window boxes, and border fronts. Grow in full sun to partial shade in well-drained soil; established plants cope well with heat and dry spells.

common_name: Little Blue Fountain Agapanthus (Dwarf Fountain-Form Lily of the Nile)

planting.note: Plant container-grown starts in spring in well-drained soil in full sun to light shade; this Southern Living Plant Collection introduction forms a fountain-like dwarf clump and is cold hardy to around 10°F once established.

directions: A dwarf, spreading selection forming low, fountain-like tufts of lush strappy foliage noticeably wider than tall, with sturdy stalks bearing deep blue, funnel-shaped flower clusters from summer into fall. Its quick-growing, dense habit suits flowering groundcover, mass planting, and containers alike, with strong drought and heat tolerance once established. Grow in full sun, filtered sun, or partial sun with moderate to regular water.

common_name: Galaxy White Agapanthus (Cold-Hardy Reblooming White Lily of the Nile)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in well-drained soil in full sun; Galaxy White is a US-patented, cold-hardy selection bred for reliable overwintering as far north as USDA zone 6.

directions: A patented hardy agapanthus bred to extend the genus into colder climates, producing generous clusters of crisp pure white flowers on sturdy stems in midsummer above tidy clumps of strap-like foliage. It reaches about three feet tall and was trialed specifically for strong winter survival well beyond the usual half-hardy limits of agapanthus. Grow in full sun in well-drained soil with moderate, regular moisture, and mulch the crown through the coldest winters.

common_name: Galaxy Blue Agapanthus (Cold-Hardy Reblooming Periwinkle Lily of the Nile)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in well-drained soil in full sun; Galaxy Blue is a US-patented (PP31,421) companion to Galaxy White bred for cold hardiness and reliable summer-long rebloom.

directions: A patented hardy selection with radiant periwinkle-blue flowers, each petal marked with a subtle darker stripe, on stems towering to around three feet above strap-like foliage. Once flowering begins in summer it continues to rebloom through the season, bred and trialed specifically for winter survival in colder gardens than most agapanthus tolerate. Grow in full sun in well-drained soil with moderate, regular water, and deadhead spent scapes to encourage continued rebloom.

common_name: Elaine Agapanthus (Robust Dark Violet-Blue Lily of the Nile)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in well-drained soil in full sun; Elaine was patented in California (US Plant Patent 7303, now expired) and is a sister seedling to the well-known cultivar Ellamae.

directions: A vigorous, large-flowered hybrid raised from Agapanthus africanus and A. praecox subsp. orientalis parentage, forming a fast-growing clump of wide, arching evergreen foliage topped by dark blue-violet, densely packed flower heads on tall scapes in midsummer. It is a sister seedling to the popular 'Ellamae', though more compact with more violet-tinged color. Grow in full sun in well-drained soil; foliage stays evergreen in mild-winter climates and the clump bulks up quickly once established.

common_name: Blush Pink Agapanthus (White-to-Pink Bicolor Lily of the Nile)

planting.note: Plant container-grown starts in spring in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; Blush Pink is one of the first agapanthus bred with genuine pink-flushed flowers and is protected under US Plant Patent 36,608.

directions: A clump-forming evergreen cultivar with trumpet-shaped flowers that open predominantly white and gradually develop soft blush-pink tones toward the petal edges as they mature, a delicate two-tone display unlike the usual blues, purples, and whites of the genus. Arching strap-like leaves support flower scapes reaching roughly two and a half feet from July through September. Grow in fertile, moist but well-drained soil in full sun or in a container; it is highly disease-resistant and well suited to borders, pots, and water-wise plantings.

common_name: Ever Poppin' Pink Agapanthus (True Pink Reblooming Lily of the Nile)

planting.note: Plant container-grown starts in spring in well-drained soil in full sun; bred by De Wet Plant Breeders and introduced through the Southern Living Plant Collection as one of the first true deep-pink agapanthus.

directions: A compact, heat- and drought-tolerant selection bred to deliver a genuinely strong pink flower color, carrying full rounded umbels of deep pink blooms through summer with reliable rebloom later in the season. Its medium-compact habit and good disease resistance suit borders and large containers alike. Grow in full sun in well-drained soil, and deadhead spent scapes to encourage a continued second flush of color.

common_name: Ever Sapphire Agapanthus (Early-Blooming Reblooming Blue Lily of the Nile)

planting.note: Plant container-grown starts in spring in well-drained soil in full sun to part shade; Ever Sapphire is part of the Southern Living Plant Collection's reblooming semi-dwarf agapanthus line.

directions: A fast-growing, semi-dwarf selection that begins flowering earlier than many agapanthus and reblooms with multiple spikes of bright blue flowers through summer. Its tough, drought-tolerant nature and compact size suit mixed borders and container plantings. Grow in full sun to partial sun in well-drained soil with moderate water, and deadhead spent flower stalks to encourage continued rebloom.

common_name: Ever Amethyst Agapanthus (Early-Blooming Reblooming Purple Lily of the Nile)

planting.note: Plant container-grown starts in spring in well-drained soil in full sun to part shade; Ever Amethyst is part of the Southern Living Plant Collection's reblooming semi-dwarf agapanthus line, a dark-purple companion to Ever Sapphire.

directions: A semi-dwarf selection that flowers earlier than many agapanthus and reblooms with repeated spikes of rich dark-purple flowers through summer. Fast growing, tough, and drought tolerant, it brings a deeper, more saturated purple tone than the typical blue-violet of the genus. Grow in full sun to partial sun in well-drained soil with moderate water, and deadhead spent flower stalks to keep successive bloom spikes coming.

common_name: Ever White Agapanthus (Compact Reblooming White Lily of the Nile)

planting.note: Plant container-grown starts in spring in well-drained soil in full sun to part shade; Ever White is a compact, multi-flush reblooming white selection from the Southern Living Plant Collection.

directions: A compact, fast-growing selection carrying clusters of pure white, trumpet-shaped flowers over an unusually long season, producing multiple flushes of bloom from early summer through fall rather than one concentrated flush. Its small mature size suits borders, containers, and landscape accents. Grow in full sun to partial shade in well-drained soil with moderate water; its compact habit makes it easy to establish in a single season.
